# DocumentedMemberAccessOnNonObject

<Badge type="warning" text="warning" /> <Badge type="tip" text="native" /> <Badge type="info" text="off by default" />

Group: [Probable bugs](/rules/#probable-bugs)

Report a method call or property access on a value that PHPDoc says is never
an object. The code may still run, since PHP does not check PHPDoc, but the
access and the documentation disagree. Receivers the code alone proves are
never objects are MemberAccessOnNonObject's.

## Example

```php{5}
<?php
/** @param int $id */
function label($id): string
{
    return $id->name;
}
```

Reported:

<ul>
<li>line 5: Access this member on an object, not int.</li>
</ul>

## Detection

- A method call or a property read or write through `->` or `?->`.
- The type of the receiver is the one PHPDoc-aware inference gives:
  `@param`, `@var`, `@return` and `@property` tags count.
- Without null, every member of that type is an int, a float, a string,
  a bool or an array.

## Exceptions (no report)

- Receivers MemberAccessOnNonObject reports.
- A receiver of unknown type, or one that may be `mixed`, `object`,
  `iterable`, `callable` or a class.
- A receiver that can only be null, which PossiblyNullAccess covers.
- A property read inside `isset()`, `empty()` or on the left of `??`,
  which PHP evaluates without complaint.
- A receiver whose PHPDoc type the code contradicts: when the code
  alone gives the receiver a type that no value of the PHPDoc type fits
  (`/** @var int $x */` over `$x = new Order()`), the tag is stale.
- `$this` inside a closure or an arrow function, which may be bound
  to an object of another class.

## Fix

None: either the access or the documentation is wrong.

## PHP versions

No gating.

## Configure

In [`custos.json`](/guide/configuration):

```json
{
  "rules": {
    "DocumentedMemberAccessOnNonObject": {
      "enabled": true
    }
  }
}
```

## Suppress

Before the statement or declaration (or the first statement of the file):

```php
// @custos-ignore DocumentedMemberAccessOnNonObject
```
